newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday on a technical correction after sharp rises in the past few days, traders said.

But the annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 13.2 percent from 13.0 percent on Wednesday due to heavy new listings on the domestic A share markets, which boosted short-term fund demand on the repo market, they said.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 3.1 million lots from 2.6 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Thursday's fall is mainly due to a technical correction with the repo rates having been pushed up sharply in the past few days," one trader said.

"In particular, the rate for the three-day contract had been pushed to a remarkable 28.50 percent on Wednesday," he said. "Due to its high level, the contract will fall again on Friday though it fell to 22.5 percent today."
A total of nine A share firms were listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges on Thursday.
Traders said they expected most of the contracts to move around current levels on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed in dull trading due to weak sentiment after weeks of downside trading with liquidity flowing into stocks, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond that matures in August 2000 rose slightly to 107.70 yuan from 107.69 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 876,210 lots from a very thin 765,977 lots.
Traders said the spot market would have difficulty overcoming its downward trend in the short-term with the withdrawal of state banks causing a huge liquidity outflow.
The banks were recently banned by Beijing from trading on the market.
